summary: Izumi Hoshi is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1986 to 1995. She served as an associate professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies from ~2001 to 2017.
Izumi Matsuda-Kiami works in linguistics and Japanology. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and held a post at the University of Washington, where she taught Qian Lin.

J. A. B. van Buitenen was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Jan Gonda at Utrecht University (~1948–1953). He held posts at Utrecht University (~1953–1956) and the University of Chicago (~1959–1979).
J. B. Disanayaka is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. In 1996, he held posts at both SOAS University of London and the University of Colombo.

J. C. Cleary worked in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Harvard University, where his doctoral supervisor was Masatoshi Nagatomi (attested 1986), and served as an instructor at Wesleyan University.
J. Estlin Carpenter was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of London (~1860–1864) and held a post at the University of Oxford from ~1889 to 1915.

J. G. de Casparis worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He taught David N. Lorenzen and held posts as a professor at Leiden University (attested 1987) and at SOAS University of London (attested 1991).

Religious studies scholar J. Gordon Melton studied at Birmingham–Southern College, Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary, and Northwestern University. He directed the Institute for the Study of American Religion (~1969) and held posts at UC Santa Barbara (~1985–2011) and Baylor University (~2011).
J. Talboys Wheeler was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Oxford and served as Assistant Secretary for the Government of India from ~1862 to 1875.

Jack Kornfield is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Dartmouth College (~1963–1967). He held a post at Spirit Rock Meditation Center around 1987 and taught Jon Kabat-Zinn and Edward Espe Brown.
Jack Laughlin is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD from McMaster University in 1999. He held a post at the University of Sudbury.

Jacob Dalton works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan in 2002 under Donald S. Lopez Jr. and held posts at Yale (2005), SOAS, and UC Berkeley (attested 2011).
Jacob Holubeck is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied under MA supervisor Kirill Jurievitch Solonin at Fo Guang University, earning a Master of Arts attested in 2013.
Jacob N. Kinnard is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held positions at the Iliff School of Theology and at William & Mary as Assistant Professor of Religion.

Jacob Samuel Speyer was an Indologist who studied under Hendrik Kern (~1868–1872). He held posts at the University of Amsterdam (1877–1889), the University of Groningen (1889–1903), and as Professor of Indology at Leiden University (1903–1913).

Jacob Wackernagel was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Theodor Benfey at the University of Göttingen (~1873–1874). He held professorships at the University of Basel (1881–1902) and the University of Göttingen (~1902–1915).

Jacqueline I. Stone specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at San Francisco State University and UCLA, later serving as a professor at Princeton University from ~1990 to 2019 and president of the SSJR (~1997–2000).

Jacqueline Suthren Hirst is a scholar in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who completed doctoral studies under Julius Lipner (attested 2005). She held a post at the University of Manchester, attested in 2005.

Jacques Bacot was a Tibetologist and linguist. He held posts at the University of Paris and at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1936–1948), and he taught Marcelle Lalou, Rolf Alfred Stein, Zuiho Yamaguchi, and Daoquan Yu.

Jacques Gernet specialized in sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, studying at the University of Algiers 1 and ENLOV. His career included posts at CNRS, Sorbonne, EHESS, Paris Diderot, and a chair at the Collège de France (1975–1992).
